Hierarchy
Too little room to read a tree. Expansion, selection and filter are retained.

Hierarchy

The most used view in Axiom, and the one carrying the most chrome. Drag a class onto another to reparent it, drag one into the empty space under the tree to move it to owl:Thing, and try to drop a class onto its own descendant to see the block. Every rule in docs/taxonomy-moves.md is implemented, not described.

Three chrome bands become one

HierarchyPanel.tsx stacks a PaneToolbar for the Classes and Properties toggle, a second PaneToolbar for the filter and the plus button, and a panel-toolbar bottom below the tree holding one button and a selection count. For a view whose entire value is how many rows you can see at once, that is three bands and a footer spent on four controls. The published policy row for this view reads "Filter/action row above tree viewport", so there is one row, 28 pixels, and everything else is in the tree.

The keyboard model was invisible

The shipped tree announces "Ctrl-click toggles a node. Shift-click selects a visible range. Ctrl+A selects all visible rows." through aria-description, which means a screen reader is told and a sighted user is not. The same three facts are now in the footer, where they cost one line of a band that was already there, and they withdraw with the footer when the pane goes shallow. Arrow keys walk and expand, Home and End jump, Enter opens Details, and the focused row is always the row the arrows will move from.

What the move rules actually do here

Hover expands a collapsed targetHold a drag over a collapsed class for a moment and it opens, so you can reach a nested destination without dropping first.
The edges scrollHold near the top or bottom of the tree during a drag and the tree scrolls, at a rate set by how close to the edge you are.
The destination is named, not just highlightedThe action row says where the class is going, or why it cannot go there. Highlight alone cannot distinguish "drop here" from "this is blocked", and the two need different answers.
Self, descendant and owl:Thing are blockedBlocked targets take the error tint and a reason. A descendant drop would make a cycle, which is the one move that cannot be undone by moving back.
One Undo reverses the moveThe footer offers it immediately after a move, because that is the moment you discover the drop landed one row off.
A multiple parent class is markedIt appears beneath its first asserted parent and carries an also under tag naming the others, so the row does not read as the whole truth. Dropping it makes the target that first parent.

What a narrow pane sheds, and what it must not

Drag the pane in and the counts lose their unit word: 412 instances becomes 412. The word is repeated on every row to say what the Classes and Properties switch above already says, so it is the cheapest thing in the row. It is not deleted, it is moved to the accessibility tree, so a screen reader still hears the unit.

That word was not the real defect, though. Everything in the row except the name was unshrinkable, so the name was the only thing flexbox could take space from, and it went to zero while a count nobody needed in full held its width and the row overflowed anyway. The name is the one reason to look at a tree. It now has a floor and truncates with an ellipsis; the count and the also under tag shrink before it does; and the indent step tightens from 13 to 9 pixels so depth stops eating the row it is describing.

What is seeded rather than read from your store

The taxonomy, the property tree and the instance counts are a fixed extract, with one multiple parent class included so that path is real. Selection, expansion, filtering, the move rules and the keyboard model all run against it.
